report.title: QQQ hedge update: partial protection through a sharper selloff
report.period_basis: Historical option snapshot and scenario analysis
report.provenance: Approved redacted summary of the dated private report. Original account evidence is not published.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.body: The working eight-put example showed an indicative gain of US$14,216, not a confirmed trading profit. The analysis used eight QQQ US$750 puts expiring 19 February 2027, a reconstructed reference premium of US$46.50 and the later displayed bid of US$64.27. Entry and exit fills were not established.

sections.heading: Visual 1: Three-stage quote and valuation table
sections.body:
| Measure | Initial reference | 30 October review | 31 October update |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| QQQ snapshot | US$721.25 | US$715.28 | US$690.53 |

| Conditional gain | US$0 | +US$4,368 | +US$14,216 |

Chart: use three separate labelled observations, not a continuous live-price series. Reference cost is reconstructed; later values are indicative bid-side marks.

sections.heading: Purpose and outcome
sections.body:
The plan was temporary protection through an earnings window, with an intended exit one week after entry. A longer option expiry was chosen to reduce estimated short-holding-period time decay. The stated purpose was protection against a repricing associated with AI capital spending, cash-flow pressure and debt-service concerns, rather than a claim that a particular company would fail.

The later update showed a larger dollar gain but a smaller proportion of the illustrative stock loss offset. The report's QQQ-equivalent portfolio comparison showed 47.68% of the reference loss offset, versus 75.39% in the earlier review. Actual stock holdings and their returns were not established.

sections.heading: Visual 2: Normalized hedge comparison
sections.body:
Normalize the stock sleeve to 100 reference units. Fund the option premium separately at 5.3143 units, so both cases start with 105.3143 total units.

| At the 31 October snapshot | Without hedge | With the assumed puts |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Stock-sleeve change | -4.2593 units | -4.2593 units |
| Hedge contribution | 0.0000 units | +2.0309 units |
| Combined change | -4.2593 units | -2.2284 units |
| Stock loss offset | 0.00% | 47.68% |

Chart: two loss bars, with the hedge contribution shown as a green bridge. Label this a normalized hypothetical portfolio, not personal account performance.

sections.heading: Costs and limitations
sections.body:
Time decay was one component of cost, not a fixed insurance bill. Starting Greeks suggested approximately US$660 of seven-day theta for the eight-put example if price and implied volatility were unchanged. Price moves, volatility changes, bid-ask spreads and execution costs could produce very different results.

These snapshots do not establish a completed one-week hedge or a realized return. The latest midpoint would imply a US$14,908 gain, but midpoint is not an assured fill. Fees, financing, dividends, tax and slippage are excluded, and a QQQ proxy cannot establish the performance of a different stock portfolio.
